1	---
2	name: login-setup
3	description: >-
4	  Integrates Xsolla Login (a.k.a. NewID) — the player identity layer that issues JWTs
5	  for the Store, Pay Station, webhooks, and the partner's own backend. Covers Publisher
6	  Account configuration (OAuth 2.0 clients, callback URLs, user data storage), the full
7	  set of authentication methods (username/password, passwordless email and SMS one-time
8	  codes, 30+ social networks via browser or native silent flow, device ID, server custom
9	  ID, silent cross-platform via Steam/Xbox Live/Epic Games/PlayStation/Meta Horizon),
10	  the choice between the Login Widget, raw Login API, and Xsolla SDKs, JWT vs OAuth 2.0
11	  protocol, server-token issuance, JWT validation against the JWKS, account linking,
12	  multi-factor authentication, password reset, and per-user attributes. Use whenever a
13	  developer says "integrate Xsolla Login", "add user authentication / sign-up / sign-in",
14	  "log in with Google/Facebook/Steam/Epic/PSN/Xbox/Meta/Quest", "passwordless email or
15	  SMS code", "Sign in with Xsolla / Xsolla ID / NewID", "set up the Login widget",
16	  "validate a user JWT", "issue a server token", "link social accounts", "two-factor /
17	  MFA / 2FA", "reset password", "shadow Login project", "cross-platform account",
18	  "main/platform account", "auth via custom ID", or any time a feature elsewhere
19	  (Store cart with `Bearer JWT`, Pay Station, webhooks granting items to a `user.id`)
20	  needs an authenticated user.
21	metadata:
22	  owner: mohammed_abujalala
23	  domain: login
24	  status: draft
25	---
26	
27	## Status
28	
29	This skill is a **draft** authored by the Login SME (@mohammed_abujalala).
30	
31	Detailed material lives in `references/`:
32	- [`references/setup-pa.md`](references/setup-pa.md) — Publisher Account configuration: standard vs shadow Login project, OAuth 2.0 clients (public, confidential, server), callback URLs, allowed origins (CORS), social providers, user data storage (Xsolla / PlayFab / Firebase / custom)
33	- [`references/integration-modes.md`](references/integration-modes.md) — Login Widget vs Login API vs Xsolla SDKs; JWT vs OAuth 2.0 protocol; client-side vs server-side calls
34	- [`references/auth-flows.md`](references/auth-flows.md) — every authentication method: classic (username/password), passwordless (email / SMS one-time code), social (browser redirect + native silent token), device ID, server custom ID, silent cross-platform (Steam / Xbox Live / Epic Games / PSN / Meta Horizon)
35	- [`references/tokens-and-validation.md`](references/tokens-and-validation.md) — user JWT vs server JWT, claims, expiration & refresh, JWKS validation, common errors, rate limits, IP allowlist
36	- [`references/user-management.md`](references/user-management.md) — user profile, password reset, MFA, account linking, social linking, attributes, friends, search, ban/unban, export/import
37	
38	## When to use
39	
40	Use this skill when the developer wants to:
41	
42	- Add user authentication to a game or web app — register/sign-in, "Continue with Google/Facebook/Steam/Epic/PSN/Xbox/Meta", passwordless email or SMS one-time code, device ID, custom ID
43	- Configure a Login project in Publisher Account: OAuth 2.0 clients, callback URLs, social providers, MFA, password policy, rate limits, custom email/SMS templates
44	- Pick between **Login Widget**, **Login API**, or an **Xsolla SDK** — and between **JWT** and **OAuth 2.0** protocols
45	- Issue and use a **server JWT** for server-to-server calls (create/import users, server-side attributes, etc.)
46	- **Validate a user JWT** in their backend (signature, `iss`, `exp`, `xsolla_login_project_id`, `groups`, `sub`)
47	- Manage users: link social accounts, reset password, enable MFA, edit profile, manage attributes, ban/unban, search, export/import
48	- Build a **shadow Login project** for cross-platform accounts (main account ↔ Steam / Xbox / Epic / PSN platform accounts)
49	- Provide a logged-in `Bearer JWT` to **Store / cart / payment-token** flows in `catalog-design`, **Headless Checkout** in `headless-checkout-integration`, or `user.id` to the handler in `webhooks-impl`
50	- **Style / theme / brand the Login UI** so the widget matches the game — hand off to [`login-styling`](../login-styling/SKILL.md)
51	
52	Out of scope: **visual styling of the Login UI (→ [`login-styling`](../login-styling/SKILL.md))**, catalog & purchase (→ `catalog-design`), Payments (→ `headless-checkout-integration`), webhook handler implementation (→ `webhooks-impl`), Xsolla account/API-key bootstrap (→ `merchant-setup`).
53	
54	## Prerequisites
55	
56	```bash
57	export XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID=<your merchant ID>
58	export XSOLLA_PROJECT_ID=<your project ID>
59	export XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY=<your API key>
60	export XSOLLA_LOGIN_PROJECT_ID=<UUID of the Login project>
61	export XSOLLA_LOGIN_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=<numeric OAuth 2.0 client ID>
62	# server flow only — never expose to client builds
63	export XSOLLA_LOGIN_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=<OAuth 2.0 client secret>
64	```
65	
66	- An Xsolla project (run `merchant-setup` first — it sets the publisher/project variables).
67	- A **Login project** created in Publisher Account → **Players → Login**, plus at least one **OAuth 2.0 client** (public for browser/mobile widget; confidential or server for backend issuance).
68	- **Xsolla MCP (strongly recommended).** Connect the official Xsolla MCP server (<https://developers.xsolla.com/get-started/ai-assistants/>). Before calling any Login API, verify the current request schema with `search_xsolla_sources` — this skill links the right operations, but field-level schemas must come from live docs, not from this file. If MCP is unavailable, fetch the linked developers.xsolla.com pages.
69	- API base URL: `https://login.xsolla.com/api`. All Login traffic is HTTPS only; HTTP is rejected.
70	
71	## Steps
72	
73	1. **Configure the Login project in Publisher Account.** Create or pick the Login project (standard for most games, **shadow** for cross-platform — Steam/Xbox/Epic/PSN — with a separate main account project). Pick the user data storage (Xsolla default, or PlayFab / Firebase / custom proxy). Add at least one **OAuth 2.0 client**: *public* for the Widget/SDK, *confidential* for backend code-exchange, *server (client_credentials)* for S2S calls. Set the **Callback URL(s)** and **Allowed origins (CORS)**. Enable the **social networks** the game needs and fill in each provider's App ID + Secret (and Organization ID for org-scoped IDs on Meta Horizon). Decide on email/phone collection, password policy, MFA, custom email/SMS templates. Full checklist: [`references/setup-pa.md`](references/setup-pa.md).
74	
75	2. **Pick the integration mode and protocol.** Default to the **Login Widget** (`@xsolla/login-sdk`) for web — ready-made UI, fastest path. Use the **Login API** directly when building a custom UI or a non-web client; use an **Xsolla SDK** (Unity / Unreal / iOS / Android / Cocos) for engines. For protocol, prefer **OAuth 2.0** (browser/mobile, refresh tokens, SSO) — fall back to JWT only when the partner has a tightly controlled environment and no need for refresh. Decision matrix and widget initialization: [`references/integration-modes.md`](references/integration-modes.md).
76	
77	3. **Implement the chosen authentication method(s).** Most projects ship at least one of: **classic** username/email + password (`Register new user` → `Auth by username and password`, plus `Reset password`); **passwordless** email or SMS (`Start auth by email/phone` → user enters one-time code → `Complete auth by email/phone`); **social** (browser: `Get link for social auth` → redirect → callback returns token; native/silent: `Auth via access token of social network` for mobile/headset apps that already have a provider token, e.g. Meta Horizon nonce, Steam session ticket, Epic exchange code); **device ID** for guest play; **server custom ID** for partner-issued IDs; **silent cross-platform** for shadow projects (Steam/Xbox/Epic/PSN session ticket → JWT). Endpoints, request shapes, and provider notes: [`references/auth-flows.md`](references/auth-flows.md).
78	
79	4. **Style the Login UI — do not ship the stock appearance.** Once the widget (or custom Login-API front end) is rendering the auth flow, theme it to match the game: colors, logo, typography, background, buttons, dark mode. **Any player-facing Login screen must be styled — invoke the [`login-styling`](../login-styling/SKILL.md) skill** for the theming mechanics. This is a required part of a real integration, not an optional polish step.
80	
81	5. **Validate the user JWT on every privileged request.** On every request to your backend that uses the user JWT, verify: signature against `https://login.xsolla.com/api/projects/{login_project_id}/keys` (JWKS), `iss == https://login.xsolla.com`, `exp` in the future, `xsolla_login_project_id == <expected>`. Cache JWKS with `kid`-aware rotation. Use `sub` (user UUID) as the user identifier — never `email` or `username`, both can change. Issue a **server JWT** with `grant_type=client_credentials` for S2S calls. Refresh user JWTs via `grant_type=refresh_token` before they expire. Full claim list, `[OAuth2.0] Generate JWT`, `Validate user JWT`, `Validate Server JWT`, error codes: [`references/tokens-and-validation.md`](references/tokens-and-validation.md).
82	
83	6. **Wire up user management features the product needs.** After the basic flow works, layer on: **profile** (`Get/Update user details`, picture, phone, email); **password reset** (`Reset password` → confirmation email → `Confirm password reset`); **MFA / 2FA** (project-level toggle + per-user setup); **social account linking** (`Get URL to link social network to account`, `Link/Delete linked network`); **account linking across projects** (`Create code for linking accounts` → `Link accounts by code`, or `Link user IDs via external ID` server-side); **attributes** (per-user JSON for save state, preferences, partner data — client-side and server-side variants); **friends**, **search**, **ban/unban**, **export/import**. Endpoint table: [`references/user-management.md`](references/user-management.md).
84	
85	7. **Verify end-to-end.** In a sandbox project: register a test user, log in with each enabled method, decode the returned JWT, verify it against the JWKS, refresh it, hit a Store call with `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>` (the catalog-design fast-purchase flow exercises this), confirm the Pay Station payment-token call accepts it, and confirm the webhook delivers the same `user.id` (= JWT `sub`) so the `webhooks-impl` handler can grant items.
86	
87	## Common pitfalls
88	
89	- **Wrong client / wrong protocol mix.** A *public* OAuth 2.0 client cannot do `client_credentials`; a *server* client cannot do user login. JWT-protocol endpoints (`/api/login/...`) and OAuth 2.0 endpoints (`/api/oauth2/...`) have different paths and parameter shapes — pick one per flow and stay consistent. See [`references/integration-modes.md`](references/integration-modes.md).
90	- **Trusting the JWT without validating it.** A JWT is just a base64 payload. Always verify signature against the **project's JWKS** (`/api/projects/{login_project_id}/keys`), not a hard-coded key, and check `iss`, `exp`, and `xsolla_login_project_id`. Without these, any forged token is accepted.
91	- **Mismatched callback URL / CORS origin.** Auth fails silently or returns `redirect_uri_mismatch` when the URL passed to the Widget/API is not exactly listed under **Callback URLs** / **Allowed origins (CORS)** in Publisher Account. Trailing slash, scheme (http vs https), and port must match byte-for-byte.
92	- **Identifying users by `email` or `username` instead of `sub`.** Both can be changed by the user (or by social-account linking) — use the JWT `sub` (UUID) as the stable internal user ID. Email/username are convenience fields only.
93	- **One-time codes / nonces retried.** Passwordless email/SMS codes and native social-auth nonces (Meta Horizon `GetUserProof`, Steam session ticket on first use) are **single-use**. A naive client retry on a transient 5xx burns the credential and the next attempt fails — request a fresh code/nonce per attempt and surface the right error. See [`references/auth-flows.md`](references/auth-flows.md).
94	- **Forgetting to refresh.** User JWTs expire (default 24 h). Without `grant_type=refresh_token` (OAuth 2.0) or re-auth (JWT protocol), Store and Pay Station calls start failing 401 mid-session. Refresh proactively before `exp`.
95	- **Shadow project confusion.** Shadow Login projects store **platform accounts** (one per Steam/Xbox/Epic/PSN), main projects store **main accounts**. Linking is one-way (platform → main); unlinking is not supported. Don't put real-money payment users in a shadow project as their primary identity. Details: [`references/setup-pa.md`](references/setup-pa.md).
96	
97	## Agent test
98	
99	Prompt: "Integrate Xsolla Login into my web game. I want a 'Continue with Google' button, classic email + password sign-up with email confirmation, and a passwordless email one-time-code option. Validate JWTs on my Node.js backend before granting access to the Store API."
100	
101	Expected (live run, sandbox): the agent reads this `SKILL.md` plus all five references, configures a standard Login project with an OAuth 2.0 *public* client + Google social provider, scaffolds Login Widget initialization in the frontend, implements the three auth flows (Google via `Get link for social auth` redirect; classic via `Register new user` → email confirmation → `Auth by username and password`; passwordless via `Start auth by email` → `Complete auth by email`), and adds an Express middleware that fetches `/api/projects/{login_project_id}/keys`, verifies signature + `iss` + `exp` + `xsolla_login_project_id`, and exposes `req.user.sub`. Sandbox smoke test: register a user → email confirmation `200` → login with each of the three methods → JWT validates → refresh succeeds → middleware rejects a tampered token with 401. ⏳ Pending live run on a fixture project.
102

  for the Store, Pay Station, webhooks, and the partner's own backend. Covers Publisher
  Account configuration (OAuth 2.0 clients, callback URLs, user data storage), the full
  set of authentication methods (username/password, passwordless email and SMS one-time
  codes, 30+ social networks via browser or native silent flow, device ID, server custom
  ID, silent cross-platform via Steam/Xbox Live/Epic Games/PlayStation/Meta Horizon),
  the choice between the Login Widget, raw Login API, and Xsolla SDKs, JWT vs OAuth 2.0
  protocol, server-token issuance, JWT validation against the JWKS, account linking,
  multi-factor authentication, password reset, and per-user attributes. Use whenever a
  developer says "integrate Xsolla Login", "add user authentication / sign-up / sign-in",
  "log in with Google/Facebook/Steam/Epic/PSN/Xbox/Meta/Quest", "passwordless email or
  SMS code", "Sign in with Xsolla / Xsolla ID / NewID", "set up the Login widget",
  "validate a user JWT", "issue a server token", "link social accounts", "two-factor /
  MFA / 2FA", "reset password", "shadow Login project", "cross-platform account",
  "main/platform account", "auth via custom ID", or any time a feature elsewhere
  (Store cart with `Bearer JWT`, Pay Station, webhooks granting items to a `user.id`)

## Status

This skill is a **draft** authored by the Login SME (@mohammed_abujalala).

Detailed material lives in `references/`:
- [`references/setup-pa.md`](references/setup-pa.md) — Publisher Account configuration: standard vs shadow Login project, OAuth 2.0 clients (public, confidential, server), callback URLs, allowed origins (CORS), social providers, user data storage (Xsolla / PlayFab / Firebase / custom)
- [`references/integration-modes.md`](references/integration-modes.md) — Login Widget vs Login API vs Xsolla SDKs; JWT vs OAuth 2.0 protocol; client-side vs server-side calls
- [`references/auth-flows.md`](references/auth-flows.md) — every authentication method: classic (username/password), passwordless (email / SMS one-time code), social (browser redirect + native silent token), device ID, server custom ID, silent cross-platform (Steam / Xbox Live / Epic Games / PSN / Meta Horizon)
- [`references/tokens-and-validation.md`](references/tokens-and-validation.md) — user JWT vs server JWT, claims, expiration & refresh, JWKS validation, common errors, rate limits, IP allowlist
- [`references/user-management.md`](references/user-management.md) — user profile, password reset, MFA, account linking, social linking, attributes, friends, search, ban/unban, export/import

## When to use

Use this skill when the developer wants to:

- Add user authentication to a game or web app — register/sign-in, "Continue with Google/Facebook/Steam/Epic/PSN/Xbox/Meta", passwordless email or SMS one-time code, device ID, custom ID
- Configure a Login project in Publisher Account: OAuth 2.0 clients, callback URLs, social providers, MFA, password policy, rate limits, custom email/SMS templates
- Pick between **Login Widget**, **Login API**, or an **Xsolla SDK** — and between **JWT** and **OAuth 2.0** protocols
- Issue and use a **server JWT** for server-to-server calls (create/import users, server-side attributes, etc.)
- **Validate a user JWT** in their backend (signature, `iss`, `exp`, `xsolla_login_project_id`, `groups`, `sub`)
- Manage users: link social accounts, reset password, enable MFA, edit profile, manage attributes, ban/unban, search, export/import
- Build a **shadow Login project** for cross-platform accounts (main account ↔ Steam / Xbox / Epic / PSN platform accounts)
- Provide a logged-in `Bearer JWT` to **Store / cart / payment-token** flows in `catalog-design`, **Headless Checkout** in `headless-checkout-integration`, or `user.id` to the handler in `webhooks-impl`
- **Style / theme / brand the Login UI** so the widget matches the game — hand off to [`login-styling`](../login-styling/SKILL.md)

Out of scope: **visual styling of the Login UI (→ [`login-styling`](../login-styling/SKILL.md))**, catalog & purchase (→ `catalog-design`), Payments (→ `headless-checkout-integration`), webhook handler implementation (→ `webhooks-impl`), Xsolla account/API-key bootstrap (→ `merchant-setup`).

## Prerequisites

```bash
export XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID=<your merchant ID>
export XSOLLA_PROJECT_ID=<your project ID>
export XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY=<your API key>
export XSOLLA_LOGIN_PROJECT_ID=<UUID of the Login project>
export XSOLLA_LOGIN_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=<numeric OAuth 2.0 client ID>
# server flow only — never expose to client builds
export XSOLLA_LOGIN_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=<OAuth 2.0 client secret>
```

- An Xsolla project (run `merchant-setup` first — it sets the publisher/project variables).
- A **Login project** created in Publisher Account → **Players → Login**, plus at least one **OAuth 2.0 client** (public for browser/mobile widget; confidential or server for backend issuance).
- **Xsolla MCP (strongly recommended).** Connect the official Xsolla MCP server (<https://developers.xsolla.com/get-started/ai-assistants/>). Before calling any Login API, verify the current request schema with `search_xsolla_sources` — this skill links the right operations, but field-level schemas must come from live docs, not from this file. If MCP is unavailable, fetch the linked developers.xsolla.com pages.
- API base URL: `https://login.xsolla.com/api`. All Login traffic is HTTPS only; HTTP is rejected.

## Steps

1. **Configure the Login project in Publisher Account.** Create or pick the Login project (standard for most games, **shadow** for cross-platform — Steam/Xbox/Epic/PSN — with a separate main account project). Pick the user data storage (Xsolla default, or PlayFab / Firebase / custom proxy). Add at least one **OAuth 2.0 client**: *public* for the Widget/SDK, *confidential* for backend code-exchange, *server (client_credentials)* for S2S calls. Set the **Callback URL(s)** and **Allowed origins (CORS)**. Enable the **social networks** the game needs and fill in each provider's App ID + Secret (and Organization ID for org-scoped IDs on Meta Horizon). Decide on email/phone collection, password policy, MFA, custom email/SMS templates. Full checklist: [`references/setup-pa.md`](references/setup-pa.md).

2. **Pick the integration mode and protocol.** Default to the **Login Widget** (`@xsolla/login-sdk`) for web — ready-made UI, fastest path. Use the **Login API** directly when building a custom UI or a non-web client; use an **Xsolla SDK** (Unity / Unreal / iOS / Android / Cocos) for engines. For protocol, prefer **OAuth 2.0** (browser/mobile, refresh tokens, SSO) — fall back to JWT only when the partner has a tightly controlled environment and no need for refresh. Decision matrix and widget initialization: [`references/integration-modes.md`](references/integration-modes.md).

3. **Implement the chosen authentication method(s).** Most projects ship at least one of: **classic** username/email + password (`Register new user` → `Auth by username and password`, plus `Reset password`); **passwordless** email or SMS (`Start auth by email/phone` → user enters one-time code → `Complete auth by email/phone`); **social** (browser: `Get link for social auth` → redirect → callback returns token; native/silent: `Auth via access token of social network` for mobile/headset apps that already have a provider token, e.g. Meta Horizon nonce, Steam session ticket, Epic exchange code); **device ID** for guest play; **server custom ID** for partner-issued IDs; **silent cross-platform** for shadow projects (Steam/Xbox/Epic/PSN session ticket → JWT). Endpoints, request shapes, and provider notes: [`references/auth-flows.md`](references/auth-flows.md).

4. **Style the Login UI — do not ship the stock appearance.** Once the widget (or custom Login-API front end) is rendering the auth flow, theme it to match the game: colors, logo, typography, background, buttons, dark mode. **Any player-facing Login screen must be styled — invoke the [`login-styling`](../login-styling/SKILL.md) skill** for the theming mechanics. This is a required part of a real integration, not an optional polish step.

5. **Validate the user JWT on every privileged request.** On every request to your backend that uses the user JWT, verify: signature against `https://login.xsolla.com/api/projects/{login_project_id}/keys` (JWKS), `iss == https://login.xsolla.com`, `exp` in the future, `xsolla_login_project_id == <expected>`. Cache JWKS with `kid`-aware rotation. Use `sub` (user UUID) as the user identifier — never `email` or `username`, both can change. Issue a **server JWT** with `grant_type=client_credentials` for S2S calls. Refresh user JWTs via `grant_type=refresh_token` before they expire. Full claim list, `[OAuth2.0] Generate JWT`, `Validate user JWT`, `Validate Server JWT`, error codes: [`references/tokens-and-validation.md`](references/tokens-and-validation.md).

6. **Wire up user management features the product needs.** After the basic flow works, layer on: **profile** (`Get/Update user details`, picture, phone, email); **password reset** (`Reset password` → confirmation email → `Confirm password reset`); **MFA / 2FA** (project-level toggle + per-user setup); **social account linking** (`Get URL to link social network to account`, `Link/Delete linked network`); **account linking across projects** (`Create code for linking accounts` → `Link accounts by code`, or `Link user IDs via external ID` server-side); **attributes** (per-user JSON for save state, preferences, partner data — client-side and server-side variants); **friends**, **search**, **ban/unban**, **export/import**. Endpoint table: [`references/user-management.md`](references/user-management.md).

7. **Verify end-to-end.** In a sandbox project: register a test user, log in with each enabled method, decode the returned JWT, verify it against the JWKS, refresh it, hit a Store call with `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>` (the catalog-design fast-purchase flow exercises this), confirm the Pay Station payment-token call accepts it, and confirm the webhook delivers the same `user.id` (= JWT `sub`) so the `webhooks-impl` handler can grant items.

## Common pitfalls

- **Wrong client / wrong protocol mix.** A *public* OAuth 2.0 client cannot do `client_credentials`; a *server* client cannot do user login. JWT-protocol endpoints (`/api/login/...`) and OAuth 2.0 endpoints (`/api/oauth2/...`) have different paths and parameter shapes — pick one per flow and stay consistent. See [`references/integration-modes.md`](references/integration-modes.md).
- **Trusting the JWT without validating it.** A JWT is just a base64 payload. Always verify signature against the **project's JWKS** (`/api/projects/{login_project_id}/keys`), not a hard-coded key, and check `iss`, `exp`, and `xsolla_login_project_id`. Without these, any forged token is accepted.
- **Mismatched callback URL / CORS origin.** Auth fails silently or returns `redirect_uri_mismatch` when the URL passed to the Widget/API is not exactly listed under **Callback URLs** / **Allowed origins (CORS)** in Publisher Account. Trailing slash, scheme (http vs https), and port must match byte-for-byte.
- **Identifying users by `email` or `username` instead of `sub`.** Both can be changed by the user (or by social-account linking) — use the JWT `sub` (UUID) as the stable internal user ID. Email/username are convenience fields only.
- **One-time codes / nonces retried.** Passwordless email/SMS codes and native social-auth nonces (Meta Horizon `GetUserProof`, Steam session ticket on first use) are **single-use**. A naive client retry on a transient 5xx burns the credential and the next attempt fails — request a fresh code/nonce per attempt and surface the right error. See [`references/auth-flows.md`](references/auth-flows.md).
- **Forgetting to refresh.** User JWTs expire (default 24 h). Without `grant_type=refresh_token` (OAuth 2.0) or re-auth (JWT protocol), Store and Pay Station calls start failing 401 mid-session. Refresh proactively before `exp`.
- **Shadow project confusion.** Shadow Login projects store **platform accounts** (one per Steam/Xbox/Epic/PSN), main projects store **main accounts**. Linking is one-way (platform → main); unlinking is not supported. Don't put real-money payment users in a shadow project as their primary identity. Details: [`references/setup-pa.md`](references/setup-pa.md).

## Agent test

Prompt: "Integrate Xsolla Login into my web game. I want a 'Continue with Google' button, classic email + password sign-up with email confirmation, and a passwordless email one-time-code option. Validate JWTs on my Node.js backend before granting access to the Store API."

Expected (live run, sandbox): the agent reads this `SKILL.md` plus all five references, configures a standard Login project with an OAuth 2.0 *public* client + Google social provider, scaffolds Login Widget initialization in the frontend, implements the three auth flows (Google via `Get link for social auth` redirect; classic via `Register new user` → email confirmation → `Auth by username and password`; passwordless via `Start auth by email` → `Complete auth by email`), and adds an Express middleware that fetches `/api/projects/{login_project_id}/keys`, verifies signature + `iss` + `exp` + `xsolla_login_project_id`, and exposes `req.user.sub`. Sandbox smoke test: register a user → email confirmation `200` → login with each of the three methods → JWT validates → refresh succeeds → middleware rejects a tampered token with 401. ⏳ Pending live run on a fixture project.

3	description: >-
4	  Integrates Xsolla Headless Checkout — a fully customizable, client-controlled
5	  payment UI built on the @xsolla/pay-station-sdk JavaScript SDK, where card data
6	  stays isolated in secure iframes and payments run through Xsolla without the
7	  standard Pay Station. Use when the developer wants to "integrate Headless Checkout",
8	  "add @xsolla/pay-station-sdk", "accept a credit card payment in sandbox",
9	  "add a payment method selector", "integrate PayPal / alternative payment methods",
10	  "add Google Pay / Apple Pay", "render psdk-card-number / psdk-payment-form",
11	  "handle onNextAction / NextAction", "do sandbox 3DS", "show payment status /
12	  psdk-status", "add a payment country selector", "change payment country",
13	  "getCountryList", "allow_modify", or "filter methods by country"
14	  for a custom checkout.
15	metadata:
16	  owner: y.klochikhin
17	  domain: payments
18	  status: draft
19	---
20	
21	## What this skill does
22	
23	Integrates Headless Checkout into a **custom checkout UI** via `@xsolla/pay-station-sdk`,
24	running in **sandbox**. This is a big integration, so it is built **one payment method at a
25	time** (see Phases) until every method works. This file is a **map and a sequence** — the actual
26	how-to lives in `references/`; load only the reference the current phase needs.
27	
28	**Frontend only.** It does **not** cover the production token backend (server-to-server) nor
29	webhook fulfillment — see `webhooks-impl` for granting items after `order_paid`.
30	
31	## When to use
32	
33	The developer wants to accept a payment with their **own** checkout UI (not the hosted Pay
34	Station) and is working in **sandbox** — standing up the integration from scratch, adding a
35	method selector, adding a payment method (card, PayPal/APM, QR, mobile), adding the Google
36	Pay / Apple Pay wallet buttons, or wiring **payment country** into the method list.
37	
38	## Prerequisites
39	
40	Run **`merchant-setup`** first. The developer must have:
41	
42	```bash
43	XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID=<your merchant ID>
44	XSOLLA_PROJECT_ID=<your project ID>
45	XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY=<your API key>   # server-side / agent-side only — NEVER ship to the browser
46	```
47	
48	If credentials are missing, stop and complete `merchant-setup` first. The **only** secret that
49	ever reaches the browser is the short-lived **payment token** — never the API key.
50	
51	## The one mental model: `form.init()` + one `onNextAction` dispatcher
52	
53	Every payment method — card, PayPal, QR, mobile, wallets — runs through the same shape: call
54	`form.init({ paymentMethodId, returnUrl })`, render the **server-driven** fields, the user
55	submits, and the SDK drives a small state machine by emitting **NextActions** to your
56	`onNextAction` handler. **React to whatever action arrives — never assume a fixed sequence, and
57	never switch on the payment method id.** All flows converge on a final **status** view.
58	
59	One dispatcher, keyed on `nextAction.type`, handles everything. Where each action is documented:
60	
61	| NextAction(s)                                                | Owned by reference     |
62	|-------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------|
63	| `show_fields`, `show_errors`, `3DS`, `check_status`         | `credit-card-form`     |
64	| `redirect`                                                  | `redirect-flow`        |
65	| `check_status`, `status_updated`                            | `payment-status`       |
66	| `special_button` (wallets)                                  | `google-pay` / `apple-pay` |
67	| `show_qr_code`, `show_mobile_payment_screen`, `show_cash_payment_instruction` | `payment-methods` |
68	
69	## Phases — build incrementally, one method at a time
70	
71	Do **not** attempt everything at once. Finish and **test** each phase in sandbox before the next.
72	
73	**Phase 1 — Credit card, end to end.** Install + `init({ sandbox: true })`, mint a sandbox token
74	(no backend), build the card form from `form.fields`, handle the `onNextAction` chain, show the
75	status, and drive a real sandbox payment including 3DS + the return page.
76	→ `initialization`, `credit-card-form`, `redirect-flow` (3DS-via-redirect), `payment-status`.
77	**Done when** the three sandbox test cards pass (see `credit-card-form` → Testing).
78	
79	**Phase 2 — Payment method selection.** Let the user pick a method instead of hardcoding the
80	card PID; hand the chosen `paymentMethodId` to `form.init()`. Choose a layout pattern (start with
81	a simple list; icons mandatory; wallets as branded buttons) and design back/retry navigation.
82	→ `payment-methods-list`. **Done when** selecting a method routes into its form.
83	
84	**Phase 3 — Additional methods, one type at a time.** Add the handlers for **redirect systems**,
85	**mobile**, **QR**, cash. But sandbox runs only redirect PS for real — mobile/QR/cash collapse to
86	the generic sandbox flow (form → notice → success), so their real UIs are **production-only**.
87	Sandbox-test on **PayPal (+ Venmo)**; code the rest to spec.
88	→ `payment-methods` (per-method NextAction; sandbox limits; PayPal/Venmo recipe), `redirect-flow`.
89	**Done when** PayPal (+ Venmo) reach a terminal status in sandbox and the other handlers are coded.
90	
91	**Phase 4 — Google Pay.** Add the wallet button via the shared dispatcher (`special_button`),
92	then **ask the user to verify and give feedback** before continuing.
93	→ `google-pay`. **Done when** a sandbox Google Pay payment completes and the user confirms.
94	
95	**Phase 5 — Apple Pay.** Same wallet pattern, then
96	**ask the user to verify and give feedback**.
97	→ `apple-pay`. **Done when** a sandbox Apple Pay payment completes and the user confirms.
98	
99	**Phase 6 — Saved methods.** Let the user save a method while paying, show saved methods as the
100	**first step** on return visits (with "pay another way" fallback), pay with one (still
101	NextAction-driven — may need CVV / 3DS), and delete them.
102	→ `saved-methods`. **Done when** the sandbox round trip passes: save → see it → pay with it → delete.
103	
104	**Phase 7 — Payment country.** Token country + store selector; pass ISO into methods /
105	`form.init` only after an explicit (or persisted) pick.
106	→ `payment-country`. **Done when** US vs JP lists differ after a pick and the choice
107	survives reload (IP auto-detect: developer checks on a real host).
108	
109	End state: every payment method integrated and working in **sandbox**, with saving/reuse and
110	country-aware methods. **Production / go-live** is Phase 7 of `shop-setup` → skill
111	`production` (contract, flip sandbox, deploy, developer live tests).
112	
113	## Styling & UX — match the store, don't ship the demo look
114	
115	Headless Checkout is an **unstyled component library**. The SDK examples use deliberately bare
116	styles — **never treat them as the target design.** From Phase 1 onward, style the checkout to
117	match the **host store's own look** (its colors, typography, radius, spacing, buttons) so it
118	reads as part of the store, not a bolted-on widget. Do this from the start — restyling a finished
119	flow is far more work than building it styled.
120	
121	Apply real **payment-UX best practices**, not a naive one-input-per-field stack. This list is
122	illustrative, not exhaustive — aim for a fast, low-friction, trustworthy checkout:
123	
124	- **Compact card entry.** Present the card as **one or two tight rows**, not a tall accordion of
125	  full-width fields. Expiry (4 digits) and CVV (3) are tiny — put them side by side on one row
126	  with the card number; don't give each a full-width block.
127	- **Auto-advance focus** to the next field as one fills (number → expiry → CVV), and surface
128	  validation **inline** next to the field, not as a distant banner.
129	- **Respect brand tokens**, keep it **responsive / mobile-first**, use accessible labels, and
130	  show clear **loading / disabled** states while the SDK works.
131	
132	The card inputs are cross-origin **secure iframes** — outer CSS cannot reach inside them, so
133	their styling goes through `setSecureComponentStyles(css)` **before** `setToken()`. Wrapper hosts
134	(`psdk-card-number`, `psdk-text`, …) are styled with normal CSS for layout/sizing. Both layers
135	and the mechanism live in `credit-card-form` → **Secure Field Styling**.
136	
137	## Testing is mandatory (every phase)
138	
139	A payment integration is verified only by a **completed sandbox transaction ending on a status
140	screen** — not by "the form renders." Each phase ends with an observed transaction; the concrete
141	test recipe lives in the phase's reference (card test matrix + headless-driving tips in
142	`credit-card-form`; PayPal sandbox login in `payment-methods`; wallet notes in `google-pay` /
143	`apple-pay`). Report the terminal screen you actually observed. **Driving it headlessly
144	(Playwright/Puppeteer)? Read [`references/testing.md`](references/testing.md) first** — the
145	cross-cutting gotchas (secure-field `fill()` vs keystrokes, submit-button host click, driver
146	artifact vs real bug) that otherwise eat hours.
147	
148	## References
149	
150	Load only what the current phase needs.
151	
152	- [`references/documentation.md`](references/documentation.md) — navigation map: which official doc / GitHub example to
153	  load per task, full component table, SDK reference (README)
154	- [`references/demo-install.md`](references/demo-install.md) — `headless-checkout-demo` (full React + Vite): the **most
155	  complete** example and **fastest to access** once installed (local file reads, no doc fetches), but requires cloning
156	  the repo locally and linking it to the agent
157	- [`references/initialization.md`](references/initialization.md) — install SDK, `init({ sandbox: true })` +
158	  `setToken()`, getting a sandbox payment token with **no backend**
159	- [`references/payment-methods-list.md`](references/payment-methods-list.md) — `psdk-payment-methods` vs custom API,
160	  `selectionChange`, handoff to `form.init()`; **layout patterns (list / accordion / tabs), method
161	  icons, wallet-button placement, back navigation**
162	- [`references/payment-country.md`](references/payment-country.md) — token country /
163	  `X-User-Ip`, store selector, when to pass ISO into methods / `form.init`
164	- [`references/credit-card-form.md`](references/credit-card-form.md) — server-driven fields, field→component mapping,
165	  `setupAndAwaitFieldsLoading`, the NextActions, two 3DS paths, **the sandbox test matrix + how to drive it headlessly**
166	- [`references/redirect-flow.md`](references/redirect-flow.md) — **all redirect mechanics**: `psdk-redirect` vs manual
167	  form, GET/POST + 414, same-tab / new-tab / WebView window strategies + iframe caveat, `isNewWindowRequired` /
168	  `isSameWindowRequired`, new-tab gesture, return page (covers 3DS-via-redirect, e-wallets, extra verification)
169	- [`references/payment-status.md`](references/payment-status.md) — `check_status`, `psdk-status` vs custom UI, the **one
170	  ** `getStatus()` rule, `status_updated`, return page
171	- [`references/payment-methods.md`](references/payment-methods.md) — which method emits which NextAction; **redirect
172	  systems** (PayPal) + **SDK / same-window** methods, **QR** (`show_qr_code`), **mobile** (`show_mobile_payment_screen`);
173	  PayPal sandbox test recipe
174	- [`references/google-pay.md`](references/google-pay.md) — the **Google Pay** wallet button via the shared dispatcher:
175	  the `special_button` action, the `show_fields` (ZIP) step a bespoke screen would drop
176	- [`references/apple-pay.md`](references/apple-pay.md) — the **Apple Pay** wallet button: renders inside
177	  `psdk-submit-button` automatically (no new NextAction), desktop QR fallback, browser-support gating, domain registration
178	- [`references/saved-methods.md`](references/saved-methods.md) — **save** a method while paying (`allowSave` field /
179	  `savePaymentMethod`), **detect + show** saved methods first (`getSavedMethods`, `psdk-saved-methods`), **pay** with one
180	  (`paymentWithSavedMethod` + `savedMethodId`, still NextAction-driven), and **delete** (`delete-mode`)
181	- [`references/testing.md`](references/testing.md) — **headless sandbox testing gotchas**: secure-field `fill()` vs real
182	  keystrokes (opposite per field), the `psdk-submit-button` host click + retry, telling a driver artifact from a real bug
183	
184	### Agent test (reference run)
185	
186	Prompt: "Integrate Xsolla Headless Checkout into my web app and let me pay with a credit card in
187	sandbox." Expected: the agent follows **Phase 1** — reads `SKILL.md`, pulls `initialization`,
188	`credit-card-form`, `redirect-flow`, and `payment-status` as each step needs them; installs
189	`@xsolla/pay-station-sdk`; initializes with `sandbox: true`; mints a sandbox token; builds the
190	card form from `form.fields`; handles the full `onNextAction` chain; and **passes the three
191	sandbox test cards** (incl. the 3DS return page) on a real run. ✅

## What this skill does

Integrates Headless Checkout into a **custom checkout UI** via `@xsolla/pay-station-sdk`,
running in **sandbox**. This is a big integration, so it is built **one payment method at a
time** (see Phases) until every method works. This file is a **map and a sequence** — the actual
how-to lives in `references/`; load only the reference the current phase needs.

**Frontend only.** It does **not** cover the production token backend (server-to-server) nor
webhook fulfillment — see `webhooks-impl` for granting items after `order_paid`.

## When to use

The developer wants to accept a payment with their **own** checkout UI (not the hosted Pay
Station) and is working in **sandbox** — standing up the integration from scratch, adding a
method selector, adding a payment method (card, PayPal/APM, QR, mobile), adding the Google
Pay / Apple Pay wallet buttons, or wiring **payment country** into the method list.

## Prerequisites

Run **`merchant-setup`** first. The developer must have:

```bash
XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID=<your merchant ID>
XSOLLA_PROJECT_ID=<your project ID>
XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY=<your API key>   # server-side / agent-side only — NEVER ship to the browser
```

If credentials are missing, stop and complete `merchant-setup` first. The **only** secret that
ever reaches the browser is the short-lived **payment token** — never the API key.

## The one mental model: `form.init()` + one `onNextAction` dispatcher

Every payment method — card, PayPal, QR, mobile, wallets — runs through the same shape: call
`form.init({ paymentMethodId, returnUrl })`, render the **server-driven** fields, the user
submits, and the SDK drives a small state machine by emitting **NextActions** to your
`onNextAction` handler. **React to whatever action arrives — never assume a fixed sequence, and
never switch on the payment method id.** All flows converge on a final **status** view.

One dispatcher, keyed on `nextAction.type`, handles everything. Where each action is documented:

| NextAction(s)                                                | Owned by reference     |
|-------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------|
| `show_fields`, `show_errors`, `3DS`, `check_status`         | `credit-card-form`     |
| `redirect`                                                  | `redirect-flow`        |
| `check_status`, `status_updated`                            | `payment-status`       |
| `special_button` (wallets)                                  | `google-pay` / `apple-pay` |
| `show_qr_code`, `show_mobile_payment_screen`, `show_cash_payment_instruction` | `payment-methods` |

## Phases — build incrementally, one method at a time

Do **not** attempt everything at once. Finish and **test** each phase in sandbox before the next.

**Phase 1 — Credit card, end to end.** Install + `init({ sandbox: true })`, mint a sandbox token
(no backend), build the card form from `form.fields`, handle the `onNextAction` chain, show the
status, and drive a real sandbox payment including 3DS + the return page.
→ `initialization`, `credit-card-form`, `redirect-flow` (3DS-via-redirect), `payment-status`.
**Done when** the three sandbox test cards pass (see `credit-card-form` → Testing).

**Phase 2 — Payment method selection.** Let the user pick a method instead of hardcoding the
card PID; hand the chosen `paymentMethodId` to `form.init()`. Choose a layout pattern (start with
a simple list; icons mandatory; wallets as branded buttons) and design back/retry navigation.
→ `payment-methods-list`. **Done when** selecting a method routes into its form.

**Phase 3 — Additional methods, one type at a time.** Add the handlers for **redirect systems**,
**mobile**, **QR**, cash. But sandbox runs only redirect PS for real — mobile/QR/cash collapse to
the generic sandbox flow (form → notice → success), so their real UIs are **production-only**.
Sandbox-test on **PayPal (+ Venmo)**; code the rest to spec.
→ `payment-methods` (per-method NextAction; sandbox limits; PayPal/Venmo recipe), `redirect-flow`.
**Done when** PayPal (+ Venmo) reach a terminal status in sandbox and the other handlers are coded.

**Phase 4 — Google Pay.** Add the wallet button via the shared dispatcher (`special_button`),
then **ask the user to verify and give feedback** before continuing.
→ `google-pay`. **Done when** a sandbox Google Pay payment completes and the user confirms.

**Phase 5 — Apple Pay.** Same wallet pattern, then
**ask the user to verify and give feedback**.
→ `apple-pay`. **Done when** a sandbox Apple Pay payment completes and the user confirms.

**Phase 6 — Saved methods.** Let the user save a method while paying, show saved methods as the
**first step** on return visits (with "pay another way" fallback), pay with one (still
NextAction-driven — may need CVV / 3DS), and delete them.
→ `saved-methods`. **Done when** the sandbox round trip passes: save → see it → pay with it → delete.

**Phase 7 — Payment country.** Token country + store selector; pass ISO into methods /
`form.init` only after an explicit (or persisted) pick.
→ `payment-country`. **Done when** US vs JP lists differ after a pick and the choice
survives reload (IP auto-detect: developer checks on a real host).

End state: every payment method integrated and working in **sandbox**, with saving/reuse and
country-aware methods. **Production / go-live** is Phase 7 of `shop-setup` → skill
`production` (contract, flip sandbox, deploy, developer live tests).

## Styling & UX — match the store, don't ship the demo look

Headless Checkout is an **unstyled component library**. The SDK examples use deliberately bare
styles — **never treat them as the target design.** From Phase 1 onward, style the checkout to
match the **host store's own look** (its colors, typography, radius, spacing, buttons) so it
reads as part of the store, not a bolted-on widget. Do this from the start — restyling a finished
flow is far more work than building it styled.

Apply real **payment-UX best practices**, not a naive one-input-per-field stack. This list is
illustrative, not exhaustive — aim for a fast, low-friction, trustworthy checkout:

- **Compact card entry.** Present the card as **one or two tight rows**, not a tall accordion of
  full-width fields. Expiry (4 digits) and CVV (3) are tiny — put them side by side on one row
  with the card number; don't give each a full-width block.
- **Auto-advance focus** to the next field as one fills (number → expiry → CVV), and surface
  validation **inline** next to the field, not as a distant banner.
- **Respect brand tokens**, keep it **responsive / mobile-first**, use accessible labels, and
  show clear **loading / disabled** states while the SDK works.

The card inputs are cross-origin **secure iframes** — outer CSS cannot reach inside them, so
their styling goes through `setSecureComponentStyles(css)` **before** `setToken()`. Wrapper hosts
(`psdk-card-number`, `psdk-text`, …) are styled with normal CSS for layout/sizing. Both layers
and the mechanism live in `credit-card-form` → **Secure Field Styling**.

## Testing is mandatory (every phase)

A payment integration is verified only by a **completed sandbox transaction ending on a status
screen** — not by "the form renders." Each phase ends with an observed transaction; the concrete
test recipe lives in the phase's reference (card test matrix + headless-driving tips in
`credit-card-form`; PayPal sandbox login in `payment-methods`; wallet notes in `google-pay` /
`apple-pay`). Report the terminal screen you actually observed. **Driving it headlessly
(Playwright/Puppeteer)? Read [`references/testing.md`](references/testing.md) first** — the
cross-cutting gotchas (secure-field `fill()` vs keystrokes, submit-button host click, driver
artifact vs real bug) that otherwise eat hours.

## References

Load only what the current phase needs.

- [`references/documentation.md`](references/documentation.md) — navigation map: which official doc / GitHub example to
  load per task, full component table, SDK reference (README)
- [`references/demo-install.md`](references/demo-install.md) — `headless-checkout-demo` (full React + Vite): the **most
  complete** example and **fastest to access** once installed (local file reads, no doc fetches), but requires cloning
  the repo locally and linking it to the agent
- [`references/initialization.md`](references/initialization.md) — install SDK, `init({ sandbox: true })` +
  `setToken()`, getting a sandbox payment token with **no backend**
- [`references/payment-methods-list.md`](references/payment-methods-list.md) — `psdk-payment-methods` vs custom API,
  `selectionChange`, handoff to `form.init()`; **layout patterns (list / accordion / tabs), method
  icons, wallet-button placement, back navigation**
- [`references/payment-country.md`](references/payment-country.md) — token country /
  `X-User-Ip`, store selector, when to pass ISO into methods / `form.init`
- [`references/credit-card-form.md`](references/credit-card-form.md) — server-driven fields, field→component mapping,
  `setupAndAwaitFieldsLoading`, the NextActions, two 3DS paths, **the sandbox test matrix + how to drive it headlessly**
- [`references/redirect-flow.md`](references/redirect-flow.md) — **all redirect mechanics**: `psdk-redirect` vs manual
  form, GET/POST + 414, same-tab / new-tab / WebView window strategies + iframe caveat, `isNewWindowRequired` /
  `isSameWindowRequired`, new-tab gesture, return page (covers 3DS-via-redirect, e-wallets, extra verification)
- [`references/payment-status.md`](references/payment-status.md) — `check_status`, `psdk-status` vs custom UI, the **one
  ** `getStatus()` rule, `status_updated`, return page
- [`references/payment-methods.md`](references/payment-methods.md) — which method emits which NextAction; **redirect
  systems** (PayPal) + **SDK / same-window** methods, **QR** (`show_qr_code`), **mobile** (`show_mobile_payment_screen`);
  PayPal sandbox test recipe
- [`references/google-pay.md`](references/google-pay.md) — the **Google Pay** wallet button via the shared dispatcher:
  the `special_button` action, the `show_fields` (ZIP) step a bespoke screen would drop
- [`references/apple-pay.md`](references/apple-pay.md) — the **Apple Pay** wallet button: renders inside
  `psdk-submit-button` automatically (no new NextAction), desktop QR fallback, browser-support gating, domain registration
- [`references/saved-methods.md`](references/saved-methods.md) — **save** a method while paying (`allowSave` field /
  `savePaymentMethod`), **detect + show** saved methods first (`getSavedMethods`, `psdk-saved-methods`), **pay** with one
  (`paymentWithSavedMethod` + `savedMethodId`, still NextAction-driven), and **delete** (`delete-mode`)
- [`references/testing.md`](references/testing.md) — **headless sandbox testing gotchas**: secure-field `fill()` vs real
  keystrokes (opposite per field), the `psdk-submit-button` host click + retry, telling a driver artifact from a real bug

### Agent test (reference run)

Prompt: "Integrate Xsolla Headless Checkout into my web app and let me pay with a credit card in
sandbox." Expected: the agent follows **Phase 1** — reads `SKILL.md`, pulls `initialization`,
`credit-card-form`, `redirect-flow`, and `payment-status` as each step needs them; installs
`@xsolla/pay-station-sdk`; initializes with `sandbox: true`; mints a sandbox token; builds the
card form from `form.fields`; handles the full `onNextAction` chain; and **passes the three
sandbox test cards** (incl. the 3DS return page) on a real run. ✅

     records only; do fulfillment on `order_*` to avoid double-granting.

- **Non-idempotent fulfillment** — granting items twice on a retried/duplicate
  webhook, or fulfilling on both `payment` and `order_paid` in separate mode.

  blocks every downstream payment webhook; the user sees an error.
- **Granting without asking how** — inventing a demo inventory while the game
  already has a real entitlement path. Always ask how the buyer receives goods
  and map the webhook user id to that system.

## Agent test

Prompt: "Implement an Xsolla webhook handler for my headless shop that grants
items after purchase. Use Node.js/Express."

Result: the agent discovered and applied this skill (read `SKILL.md` + references,
including `testing.md` / fixtures), asked how goods are granted in the product,
scaffolded a raw-body Express endpoint, and smoke-tested with fixture POSTs:
`lowercase(sha1(rawBody + secret))` rejecting tampered bodies with
`400 INVALID_SIGNATURE`; `user_validation` returning `204`/`400 INVALID_USER`;
idempotent `order_paid` granting (replay returned `2xx` with no re-grant); no
double-grant in separate mode (`payment` recorded only); `5xx` reserved for
transient errors. ✅

|-----------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

```bash
      \"currency\": \"USD\",
      \"language\": \"en\",
```

```typescript
import {headlessCheckout} from '@xsolla/pay-station-sdk';

// Read token from URL or constant
```

1	# Integration modes — Widget vs Login API vs SDKs, JWT vs OAuth 2.0
2	
3	Two orthogonal choices: **how** to call Xsolla Login (Widget / API / SDK) and **which
4	protocol** to use (JWT or OAuth 2.0).
5	
6	## How to call Login
7	
8	| Option | Best for | Pros | Cons |
9	|--------|----------|------|------|
10	| **Login Widget** (`@xsolla/login-sdk`) | Web apps, fastest UX | Ready-made UI, themable, all auth methods exposed via toggles, MFA / passwordless / social handled for you | Web only |
11	| **Login API** (raw HTTPS) | Custom UI, non-web clients, headless flows, server-side | Full control of the UI and request shape, language-agnostic | You build every screen and handle every error |
12	| **Xsolla SDK** (Unity / Unreal / iOS / Android / Cocos / …) | Engine integrations | Idiomatic per engine, wraps the API + token storage + refresh | Platform-specific quirks; one SDK version per platform |
13	
14	Decision flow:
15	
16	```
17	Web app, ship fast?                  → Login Widget
18	Web app, custom UI?                  → Login API (browser) + Widget for social pop-ups
19	Mobile/desktop game, has an engine?  → Xsolla SDK for that engine
20	Mobile/desktop game, custom engine?  → Login API + native social SDKs
21	Server-side only (S2S)?              → Login API with server OAuth 2.0 client
22	```
23	
24	## Which protocol — JWT vs OAuth 2.0
25	
26	Both protocols ultimately deliver a JWT to your client. The difference is how it is
27	issued and renewed.
28	
29	| | JWT (legacy) | OAuth 2.0 (preferred) |
30	|---|---|---|
31	| Endpoint family | `/api/login/...`, `/api/social/...` | `/api/oauth2/...` |
32	| Token returned | User JWT directly | `code` → exchange via `Generate JWT` for `access_token` (+ optional `refresh_token`) |
33	| Refresh | Re-authenticate | `grant_type=refresh_token` |
34	| Server JWT (S2S) | Not supported | `grant_type=client_credentials` |
35	| SSO | Limited | Full (`OAuth 2.0 authorize`, `Check user authentication`, `Log user out`, `Clear SSO`) |
36	| Recommended? | Only when locked-in to legacy | **Yes — default** |
37	
38	**Default to OAuth 2.0 unless the partner explicitly needs the JWT-protocol shape.** Most
39	new integrations have refresh-token requirements that make JWT-protocol painful.
40	
41	OAuth 2.0 reference: [Connecting OAuth 2.0](https://developers.xsolla.com/authenticate-users/login/security/connecting-oauth2/).
42	
43	## Login Widget initialization
44	
45	Minimal Widget config (copy the values from Publisher Account, see [`setup-pa.md`](setup-pa.md)):
46	
47	```js
48	import { Widget } from '@xsolla/login-sdk';
49	
50	const xl = new Widget({
51	  projectId:       'XSOLLA_LOGIN_PROJECT_ID',     // Login project UUID
52	  preferredLocale: 'en_US',
53	  clientId:        'XSOLLA_LOGIN_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID', // OAuth 2.0 public client
54	  responseType:    'code',
55	  state:           'CSRF-RANDOM-STRING',           // anti-CSRF, verify on callback
56	  redirectUri:     'https://your.site/callback',   // must be in Callback URLs
57	  scope:           'offline email',                // offline → issues refresh_token
58	});
59	
60	xl.open(document.getElementById('login-button'));
61	```
62	
63	After redirect, exchange the `code` query parameter for a JWT via `[OAuth2.0] Generate
64	JWT` (see [`tokens-and-validation.md`](tokens-and-validation.md)).
65	
66	For the Widget to display the right buttons, the matching toggles must be enabled in
67	Publisher Account first — Widget is purely a UI layer over the same auth methods.
68	
69	## Login API call shape
70	
71	**Base URL**: `https://login.xsolla.com/api`. All requests use HTTPS, JSON in/out.
72	
73	Auth headers:
74	
75	| Caller | Header |
76	|--------|--------|
77	| Anonymous (registration, login start) | none |
78	| Authenticated user (profile, etc.) | `Authorization: Bearer <user_JWT>` |
79	| Server (S2S, e.g. import users, server attributes) | `X-SERVER-AUTHORIZATION: <server_JWT>` |
80	
81	Project / client identifiers in query parameters:
82	
83	- JWT-protocol calls: `?projectId=<XSOLLA_LOGIN_PROJECT_ID>`
84	- OAuth 2.0 calls: `?client_id=<XSOLLA_LOGIN_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID>` (+ `redirect_uri`,
85	  `state`, `response_type`, `scope` on flows that start the auth)
86	
87	Always pass through the user's IP for rate-limit / geolocation correctness — the
88	Login service uses it for brute-force scoring and for resolving country-specific rules.
89	
90	## Where Login fits in the broader integration
91	
92	Login issues the JWT that the rest of the stack consumes:
93	
94	```
95	                     ┌────────────────────┐
96	   user JWT (Bearer) │                    │  same JWT used by:
97	   ──────────────────►   Store API        │  · catalog-design (cart, fast purchase)
98	                     │  Payments          │  · headless-checkout-integration (payment-token call)
99	                     │  Webhooks          │  · webhooks-impl (user.id == JWT.sub)
100	                     │  Partner backend   │
101	                     └────────────────────┘
102	```
103	
104	Refresh proactively before `exp` so Store/Pay-Station calls don't 401 mid-checkout.
105	
106	## When to mix
107	
108	It is normal to combine modes — for example, the Widget for the auth UI, raw Login API
109	on your backend for `Validate user JWT` and server-side user management, and SDK calls
110	on a mobile companion app. They share the same Login project, the same OAuth 2.0
111	clients, and the same user database — there is no per-mode account silo.
112

|---|---|---|
| Endpoint family | `/api/login/...`, `/api/social/...` | `/api/oauth2/...` |
| Token returned | User JWT directly | `code` → exchange via `Generate JWT` for `access_token` (+ optional `refresh_token`) |
| Refresh | Re-authenticate | `grant_type=refresh_token` |
| Server JWT (S2S) | Not supported | `grant_type=client_credentials` |
| SSO | Limited | Full (`OAuth 2.0 authorize`, `Check user authentication`, `Log user out`, `Clear SSO`) |
| Recommended? | Only when locked-in to legacy | **Yes — default** |

**Default to OAuth 2.0 unless the partner explicitly needs the JWT-protocol shape.** Most
new integrations have refresh-token requirements that make JWT-protocol painful.

OAuth 2.0 reference: [Connecting OAuth 2.0](https://developers.xsolla.com/authenticate-users/login/security/connecting-oauth2/).

## Login Widget initialization

Minimal Widget config (copy the values from Publisher Account, see [`setup-pa.md`](setup-pa.md)):

```js
import { Widget } from '@xsolla/login-sdk';

const xl = new Widget({
  projectId:       'XSOLLA_LOGIN_PROJECT_ID',     // Login project UUID
  preferredLocale: 'en_US',
  clientId:        'XSOLLA_LOGIN_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID', // OAuth 2.0 public client
  responseType:    'code',
  state:           'CSRF-RANDOM-STRING',           // anti-CSRF, verify on callback
  redirectUri:     'https://your.site/callback',   // must be in Callback URLs
  scope:           'offline email',                // offline → issues refresh_token
});

xl.open(document.getElementById('login-button'));
```

After redirect, exchange the `code` query parameter for a JWT via `[OAuth2.0] Generate
JWT` (see [`tokens-and-validation.md`](tokens-and-validation.md)).

For the Widget to display the right buttons, the matching toggles must be enabled in
Publisher Account first — Widget is purely a UI layer over the same auth methods.

## Login API call shape

**Base URL**: `https://login.xsolla.com/api`. All requests use HTTPS, JSON in/out.

Auth headers:

| Caller | Header |
|--------|--------|
| Anonymous (registration, login start) | none |
| Authenticated user (profile, etc.) | `Authorization: Bearer <user_JWT>` |
| Server (S2S, e.g. import users, server attributes) | `X-SERVER-AUTHORIZATION: <server_JWT>` |

Project / client identifiers in query parameters:

- JWT-protocol calls: `?projectId=<XSOLLA_LOGIN_PROJECT_ID>`
- OAuth 2.0 calls: `?client_id=<XSOLLA_LOGIN_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID>` (+ `redirect_uri`,
  `state`, `response_type`, `scope` on flows that start the auth)

Always pass through the user's IP for rate-limit / geolocation correctness — the
Login service uses it for brute-force scoring and for resolving country-specific rules.

## Where Login fits in the broader integration

Login issues the JWT that the rest of the stack consumes:

```
                     ┌────────────────────┐
   user JWT (Bearer) │                    │  same JWT used by:
   ──────────────────►   Store API        │  · catalog-design (cart, fast purchase)
                     │  Payments          │  · headless-checkout-integration (payment-token call)
                     │  Webhooks          │  · webhooks-impl (user.id == JWT.sub)
                     │  Partner backend   │
                     └────────────────────┘
```

Refresh proactively before `exp` so Store/Pay-Station calls don't 401 mid-checkout.

## When to mix

It is normal to combine modes — for example, the Widget for the auth UI, raw Login API
on your backend for `Validate user JWT` and server-side user management, and SDK calls
on a mobile companion app. They share the same Login project, the same OAuth 2.0
clients, and the same user database — there is no per-mode account silo.

1	# Credit Card Form
2	
3	Guide for an AI agent. The most complex Headless Checkout integration — dynamic fields, multi-step flows, two 3DS paths,
4	secure iframes.
5	
6	**Prerequisites:** `initialization` + `payment-methods-list` (or hardcode `paymentMethodId: 1380` for sandbox cards).
7	
8	---
9	
10	## Required Page Structure
11	
12	Every checkout page (by contract):
13	
14	```html
15	
16	<psdk-total></psdk-total>
17	<psdk-legal></psdk-legal>
18	```
19	
20	**Render `psdk-payment-form-messages`** (see **Form Messages** below — it carries real
21	server text like the sandbox "no redirect" notice; render it *visibly*, not hidden).
22	Optional: `psdk-finance-details`.
23	
24	**Return page** (`returnUrl`) — user lands here after 3DS redirect. Must re-run `init()` + `setToken(tokenFromUrl)` +
25	render `psdk-status`.
26	
27	---
28	
29	## Step 1: Initialize Card Form
30	
31	```typescript
32	const form = await headlessCheckout.form.init({
33	    paymentMethodId: 1380,           // sandbox card PID; use selectionChange id in production
34	    returnUrl: `${origin}/payment/return?token=${token}`,
35	    country: 'US',                   // optional; affects visible fields
36	    paymentMethodSettings: {
37	        useSingleExpirationDateField: true,  // single MM/YY field instead of month+year
38	    },
39	    overrideFormFields: {
40	        allowSubscription: {initialValue: '1'},  // pre-check save-card checkbox
41	    },
42	});
43	
44	headlessCheckout.form.onNextAction(handleNextAction);
45	```
46	
47	`form.init()` returns `{ fields, submitButtonText, isFormAutoSubmitted }`. Field set is **server-driven** — never
48	hardcode which fields exist; always read `form.fields` or react to `show_fields`.
49	
50	---
51	
52	## Step 2: Map Fields to Components
53	
54	Server returns `Field[]` with `type`, `name`, `isMandatory`. Map each field:
55	
56	| Field condition          | Component          | Attributes                 |
57	|--------------------------|--------------------|----------------------------|
58	| `name === 'card_number'` | `psdk-card-number` | `name`, `icon="true"`      |
59	| `name === 'phone'`       | `psdk-phone`       | `name`, `showFlags="true"` |
60	| `type === 'text'`        | `psdk-text`        | `name`                     |
61	| `type === 'select'`      | `psdk-select`      | `name`                     |
62	| `type === 'check'`       | `psdk-checkbox`    | `name`                     |
63	| `type === 'label'`       | **none — skip it** | —                          |
64	
65	`form.fields` is **already the visible set** (the SDK drops hidden `fix_*` / `signature`
66	fields) — render all of it, mapping **by `type`**. The one rule: **skip `type: 'label'`;
67	never fall through to a catch-all `else → psdk-text`** — a label has no secure config, so
68	`psdk-text` throws `Could not load control component config`, and a rendered
69	`termsAndConditions` is the "EULA on every step" bug. Labels are shown elsewhere: legal by
70	`psdk-legal`, status/info text (e.g. the sandbox "no redirect" notice) by
71	`psdk-payment-form-messages` (**Form Messages** below) — not as fields. Filtering to
72	`isMandatory === '1'` is an optional minimal-UI choice, not required.
73	
74	Then add `psdk-submit-button` and call **`form.activate()`**. `activate()` is
75	**mandatory, not optional** — it wires up the mounted secure fields and enables
76	submit. **Without it the form renders fine but clicking submit does nothing** (no
77	NextAction fires, no error) — a silent dead end that is easy to misread as "the SDK
78	is broken." Call it once, after the field components and the submit button are in
79	the DOM. The canonical `examples/credit-card/init-payment-flow.js` omits this call;
80	do not treat that example as complete on this point.
81	
82	---
83	
84	## Step 3: Show a loader (there is no "loading" event)
85	
86	**Trap:** `onNextAction` reports *outcomes*, not loading — the SDK gives you **no
87	"request in flight" event**. If you don't drive loaders yourself, the buyer stares at a blank
88	area during every round-trip. Two gaps:
89	
90	- **Form fetch + field load** (`form.init`, and each `show_fields` step): show a loader from
91	  the moment you start until the fields are ready. Readiness = the
92	  **`setupAndAwaitFieldsLoading(fields)` promise resolving**. Hide the form area meanwhile and
93	  reveal on resolve (mount the fields behind the loader so they load while hidden).
94	- **Submit → next action:** `psdk-submit-button` shows its **own** in-button loader — leave
95	  that gap to it.
96	
97	```typescript
98	// mount the field components FIRST (Step 2), then:
99	await headlessCheckout.form.setupAndAwaitFieldsLoading(tracked); // resolve → hide loader, reveal form
100	```
101	
102	`psdk-payment-form` does this internally; render fields manually → you call it. **Mount the
103	components before calling, and pass only the ones you mounted as secure inputs** (never a
104	`label`/hidden field) — otherwise the promise **hangs forever** on an iframe that never
105	appears. (`activate()`, not this, enables submit — Step 2.) `AbortSignal` on method switch.
106	
107	---
108	
109	## Step 4: Handle NextActions (Critical)
110	
111	Subscribe **before or right after** `form.init()`. Card flow uses these actions:
112	
113	| Action         | Meaning                                                | Handler                                                                                                                |
114	|----------------|--------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
115	| `show_fields`  | New/replacement fields (BR 2nd step, validation retry) | **Clear container**, set `form.fields = nextAction.data.fields`, re-render. Update button text from `submitButtonText` |
116	| `show_errors`  | Validation/server error                                | Display `nextAction.data.errors[0].message`                                                                            |
117	| `redirect`     | 3DS via acquirer / external MPI                        | Redirect to bank; use `psdk-redirect` or manual form submit                                                            |
118	| `3DS`          | MPI challenge flow                                     | Show `psdk-3ds` with `data-challenge={JSON.stringify(action.data.data)}` — payload is **nested** under `.data.data`   |
119	| `check_status` | Payment done                                           | Show `psdk-status`                                                                                                     |
120	
121	On `show_fields`: **clear container** → `form.fields = nextAction.data.fields` → re-render → update `submitButtonText`.
122	See `credit-card/init-payment-flow.js`, `/card-second-step`.
123	
124	**Quirk:** `show_errors` + `show_fields` may fire in sequence on failed submit. Use `AbortSignal` with
125	`setupAndAwaitFieldsLoading` if awaiting on each `show_fields`.
126	
127	---
128	
129	## Step 5: 3-D Secure (Two Paths)
130	
131	Bank chooses verification type — handle **both**:
132	
133	**`redirect`** — acquirer / external MPI. Prefer `psdk-redirect` with `data-redirect={JSON.stringify(redirect)}` —
134	handles GET/POST + new tab. If `isNewWindowRequired` — open only on user click. Full redirect mechanics (GET/POST + 414,
135	`isNewWindowRequired` / `isSameWindowRequired`, the new-tab gesture rule, return page) live in
136	[`redirect-flow.md`](redirect-flow.md) — the same `redirect` action also drives e-wallets / APMs and extra
137	verification, so it's documented once there. Refs: `/card` (step machine), `/card-3ds-custom-status` (popup +
138	`status_updated`).
139	
140	**`3DS`** — MPI challenge: `psdk-3ds` + `data-challenge={JSON.stringify(action.data.data)}` (payload is **nested** in
141	`.data.data`, not `.data`). On `threeDsWindowClosed` → re-init form (`/card`). User returns via `returnUrl` →
142	`psdk-status`.
143	
144	---
145	
146	## Step 6: Secure Field Styling
147	
148	Card inputs live in iframes — **two layers**:
149	
150	1. **Wrapper CSS** — size/position of `psdk-card-number`, `psdk-text` host elements
151	2. **Iframe styles** — `setSecureComponentStyles(cssString)` **before** `setToken()`
152	
153	Call `setSecureComponentStyles(css)` **before** `setToken()`. Ref: `secure-component-styles` example. Wrapper sizing on
154	`psdk-*` hosts; iframe styles via `setSecureComponentStyles`.
155	
156	**Also:** `cardBinCountryChanged` on `psdk-card-number` (hide fields by BIN country); `psdk-payment-form` auto-creates
157	missing fields (watch console); reset form on method switch (
158	demo); [test cards](https://developers.xsolla.com/doc/pay-station/testing/test-cards/) for 3DS/success/decline. The
159	**"save this card" checkbox** is the server-driven `allowSave` field (present only for savable methods) — see
160	`saved-methods` for saving/reusing a method.
161	
162	---
163	
164	## Form Messages (server status / info text)
165	
166	Some server responses carry a **`messages`** block — free-text status/info **not** in
167	`form.fields` and **not** a NextAction (e.g. sandbox: *"Unlike with real payment… no
168	redirect to the payment system"*). Surface it by mounting **`psdk-payment-form-messages`**
169	(it auto-subscribes to `formMessagesChanged` and renders the text — just mount it):
170	
171	```html
172	<psdk-payment-form-messages></psdk-payment-form-messages>
173	```
174	
175	**Render it visibly and keep it mounted through the whole form flow** — not `sr-only`, and
176	not only on step 1 (the message often arrives after the first submit). Hiding it is why a
177	step looks empty for no reason. Ref: `demo-install` → `.../checkout/form-container`.
178	
179	---
180	
181	## Testing (Sandbox) — you are NOT done until a real transaction lands on `psdk-status`
182	
183	Rendering the form is **not** "done." "The form renders" / "it should work" does not count — drive an actual sandbox
184	payment and observe the terminal screen. Run **all three** cards below and report the result of each. For all cards:
185	**Exp. date `12/40`**, **CVV2 any 3 digits**.
186	
187	| # | Card number        | Path exercised                          | Expected terminal state                                              |
188	|---|--------------------|-----------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
189	| 1 | `4111111111111111` | plain card, **no 3DS**                  | `check_status` → `psdk-status` shows **success**                    |
190	| 2 | `4111111111111152` | 3DS — acquirer's built-in mechanism     | `redirect` → Xsolla verify page → **return page** → success        |
191	| 3 | `4423610000000007` | 3DS — external MPI                      | `redirect` → Xsolla verify page → **return page** → success        |
192	
193	**Card 1 alone does NOT prove the integration** — it skips `redirect` and the **return page** entirely, which is the
194	part most likely to be broken (wrong `returnUrl`, SDK not loaded on the return route, stripped query params). Cards 2
195	and 3 are **mandatory**.
196	
197	**3DS flow (cards 2 & 3):** the form triggers a `redirect` to the Xsolla verify page
198	(`sandbox-secure.xsolla.com/pages/sandbox`); the password is **pre-filled** — just confirm. The user is then redirected
199	to the **return page** (`returnUrl`), where `init()` + `setToken(tokenFromUrl)` + `psdk-status` report the final status.
200	To test the **`failed`** status, enter a **wrong password** (e.g. `123456`) instead of confirming the pre-filled one.
201	
202	**Driving it headlessly.** The card inputs live in cross-origin secure iframes, but Playwright/Puppeteer can drive them:
203	
204	- Locate each input via `frameLocator('iframe[src*="text-input/<field>"]').locator('input')`.
205	- **Type with real key presses, not `fill()`.** `fill()` sets the value in one shot and the secure field's listeners
206	  never fire, so the field stays `INVALID` and **submit silently hangs** (no NextAction, no error). Use
207	  `pressSequentially(value)` / character-by-character `type()` so each keystroke registers and the field goes `VALID`.
208	- Then click the button inside `psdk-submit-button`.
209	- On the verify page: a **GDPR overlay** intercepts clicks — dismiss it first (`button.gdpr-accept-all-button`); the
210	  code is pre-filled, so click `#xps-submit-button` to confirm (or replace it with a wrong code for the `failed` path).
211	- Finally, assert the return page renders `psdk-status` with the expected terminal state and capture the screen.
212	
213	---
214	
215	## Anti-Patterns
216	
217	1. **Do not** hardcode field list without checking `form.fields` — BR/JP cards need extra steps.
218	2. **Do not** append fields on `show_fields` — **clear and re-render** the container.
219	3. **Do not** skip `returnUrl` — 3DS redirect fails without it.
220	4. **Do not** auto-redirect when `isNewWindowRequired` — use button + `psdk-redirect`.
221	5. **Do not** style card inputs only with outer CSS — use `setSecureComponentStyles`.
222	6. **Do not** ignore `show_errors` — user sees silent failure.
223	7. **Do not** call `form.init()` twice on same page without cleanup.
224	
225	---
226	
227	## Checklist
228	
229	- [ ] `psdk-total` + `psdk-legal`; `form.init` + all five NextActions handled
230	- [ ] `card_number` → `psdk-card-number`; `show_fields` clears + re-renders
231	- [ ] Map `form.fields` by `type`; **skip `label`** (no catch-all `else → psdk-text`) — labels are `psdk-legal` / form-messages, not inputs
232	- [ ] `psdk-payment-form-messages` rendered **visibly** + kept mounted (server status/info text)
233	- [ ] Loader on form fetch + each `show_fields` step (driven by `setupAndAwaitFieldsLoading`); submit gap left to the button
234	- [ ] 3DS path (`psdk-redirect` / `psdk-3ds`); return page with `psdk-status`
235
